editorial:
Imagine a guy who is so obsessed with a gross movie that he decides to make his own version in real life. That is exactly what you get with Martin. He is a lonely, creepy man who works at a warehouse and spends his free time dreaming up a way to stitch twelve people together. Unlike the first movie, this one is shot in black and white, which makes the whole thing feel cold and mean. You can tell right away that this is not a movie for everyone, as it focuses on a man who has completely lost his mind and does not care who he hurts.

What really sticks with you is how gross the practical effects are. The acting is mostly silent, but the expressions on the victims' faces make the horror feel real. It is a slow burn that gets more intense as the pile of people grows. If you have a strong stomach and love extreme horror, you should definitely check it out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch, or if you are a die-hard collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: At the end, Martin finally finishes his twelve-person chain, but things go wrong. The people in the chain fight back and eventually kill him. However, the movie ends on a dark note. It shows that the horror does not truly stop because the trauma stays with the survivors. The twist is simply that Martin's obsession leads to his own death, but he still manages to ruin many lives before he goes.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves extreme horror and gore.
